tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of Records of Arrest, Plea, Trial or Conviction (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.140)

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 610.140 is Missouri's general expungement mechanism and the route most participants belong on. It was read in full from the Revisor's current text, effective 1 January 2025. Subsection 2(1) lets any person apply to any court in which the person was charged or found guilty for an order to expunge records of that arrest, plea, trial or conviction; subsection 1(1) defines "court" as any Missouri municipal, associate circuit or circuit court, and subsection 1(2) defines "crime" as any offense, violation or infraction of Missouri state, county, municipal or administrative law. Subsection 2(2) requires the petitioner to list every crime sought to be expunged in the one petition and bars any crime excluded under subsection 3. Subsection 6 sets the six criteria the court may consider: at the time the petition is filed at least three years for a felony or one year for a misdemeanor, municipal violation or infraction has run from the date the petitioner completed any authorized disposition imposed under § 557.011; during that same period the petitioner has not been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony, excluding traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307; all obligations relating to the disposition are satisfied including fines and restitution; no charges are pending; the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to public safety; and the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it. A pleading that the petitioner meets criteria (5) and (6) creates a rebuttable presumption so long as (1) to (4) are satisfied, and the burden then shifts to the prosecuting or circuit attorney; a victim has an opportunity to be heard and the court may find that the continuing impact on the victim rebuts the presumption. The clerk gives notice to the prosecuting attorney, whose written objection is due within thirty days after receipt of service, and the court holds a hearing within sixty days after a written objection unless the parties agree otherwise. Subsection 8 makes relief mandatory once the criteria are met and requires an order of expungement or of dismissal within six months of filing. Subsection 12 dismisses a petition where the criteria are not met or false information was knowingly provided, and bars a further petition until a year has passed since the date of filing the previous one. Subsection 13 caps a lifetime at not more than three misdemeanor offenses or ordinance violations carrying an authorized term of imprisonment and not more than two felony offenses, with no limit on infractions, and subsection 2(3) lets crimes committed as part of the same course of criminal conduct go in a single petition and count only at the highest level. Subsection 14 requires the court to make a form available for pro se petitioners carrying the declaration under penalty of perjury, which is what CR360 is. Expungement here is closure under § 610.120, never destruction.

exclusions: Class A felonies (§ 610.140.3(1)).
Dangerous felonies as defined in § 556.061 (§ 610.140.3(2)).
Any offense requiring registration as a sex offender (§ 610.140.3(3)).
Any felony offense where death is an element of the offense (§ 610.140.3(4)).
Felony assault offenses, misdemeanor or felony domestic assault offenses, and felony kidnapping (§ 610.140.3(5)).
The specifically enumerated chapter 566 sex offenses and the listed offenses in other chapters (§ 610.140.3(6)).
Offenses eligible under § 610.130, so the first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense occupies its own lane and never routes here (§ 610.140.3(7)).
Intoxication-related traffic offenses and intoxication-related boating offenses, and operating an aircraft with an excessive blood alcohol content or while intoxicated (§ 610.140.3(8)).
Any ordinance violation substantially equivalent to an excluded offense (§ 610.140.3(9)).
Any offense of a motor vehicle law or ordinance committed by a person holding, or required to hold, a commercial driver's license (§ 610.140.3(10)).
Most unlawful use of weapons offenses under § 571.030, subject to the specific statutory exceptions (§ 610.140.3(11)).

A crime prosecuted outside Missouri or outside the jurisdiction of a Missouri court. § 610.140.2(2) reaches only crimes that occurred within Missouri and were prosecuted under the jurisdiction of a Missouri court.

A person whose § 610.140.13 lifetime caps are already exhausted, counting expungements granted under § 610.140 and, from the date § 610.141 becomes operative, automatic expungements granted under § 610.141 as well (§ 610.141.6 makes the caps combined).
Arrest-only records with no charge filed, which run on the separate § 610.140.7 route recorded as mo-610-140-arrest.

waitingPeriods.duration: Three years. Measured at the time the petition is filed, running back from the date the petitioner completed any authorized disposition imposed under § 557.011 — not from the arrest date and not from the conviction date.
One year, measured the same way: at the time the petition is filed, from the date the petitioner completed the authorized disposition.

The same three-year or one-year period, and the direction matters. The period runs backward from the filing of the petition, not forward from completion of the sentence. During it the petitioner must not have been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony, excluding traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307.

geography.venue: Any Missouri municipal, associate circuit or circuit court in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty (§ 610.140.1(1) and 2(1)). Rule 155.01 commences the action by filing a petition in the circuit court of the county in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty. Where the participant's crimes were charged in more than one county the petition cannot reach them all: § 610.140.2(2) requires every crime in one petition but subsection 2(1) fixes venue by court of charge or finding of guilt, so a multi-county record is a self-help stop rather than a routing choice LegalEase makes.

destination.name: Clerk of the Missouri court where the petitioner was charged or found guilty
destination.detail: Filed with the clerk of the municipal, associate circuit or circuit court where the crimes were charged or the finding of guilt entered. Missouri has forty-six judicial circuits covering 114 counties and the City of St. Louis, plus municipal divisions. The clerk assigns the case number, gives notice of the filing to the prosecuting attorney under § 610.140.6, and distributes the order under § 610.140.8. Local filing practice, copy counts and fees are confirmed with that clerk and are not optional.

components.notes: The current statewide petition, SJRC (10-24) CR360, two pages and eighty-two AcroForm fields. It is the form § 610.140.14 requires the court to make available for pro se petitioners. LegalEase completes the caption's judicial circuit and county, the petitioner's full name, date of birth, sex, race and ethnicity, current address and driver licence number and issuing state, the defendant agency selections and free-text agency lines from the participant's own records, and the offense table of case number, court name, approximate date of charge, county or municipality of charge and description of charge. Sworn paragraphs 1 to 4 are recited from the participant's answers about time elapsed, clean period, satisfied obligations and pending charges. Paragraph 6's prior-expungement disclosure is the participant's own statement and its case-number line is theirs to complete. Paragraphs 5 and 7 — that the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to public safety, and that the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it — are conclusions, are left to the participant, and are never asserted or drafted by LegalEase. The declaration under penalty of perjury and the signature line are left blank. The obsolete OSCA (11-17) CR360 in the corpus, which recites seven years for felonies and three years for misdemeanors and cites § 610.140.5.1, is never generated.

Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet — Non-Domestic Relations, four pages and 111 AcroForm fields, mandatory with a new case filing and confidential in itself. Case type code X5, Expungement of Records (610.140 RSMo), taken from the Case Types List's circuit column rather than inferred from a track name. The full Social Security number is required under Operating Rule 4.07 where the party is a person and it is reasonably available, and the sheet's own note records that the day and month of birth, the Social Security number and confidential addresses are not published through Case.net. The full Social Security number goes here and is not repeated on CR360, which does not ask for it. Each respondent named as a defendant on CR360 is entered in its own party box as an organization with party type code RES; more than one sheet may be needed.

components.conditionDescription: Generated where the participant's court expects the petitioner to tender a proposed judgment. Missouri circuits differ: some clerks and judges prepare the judgment themselves under Rule 155.05, others expect it with the petition.
components.notes: Judgment and Order of Expungement — Section 610.140 RSMo, CR370, the companion order form the Office of the State Courts Administrator publishes alongside CR360 and which Missouri circuit clerks list in their own form indexes. The review recorded this companion as not obtained and left it as an open item; it exists, it is numbered, and it is now identified. LegalEase completes only the caption, the petitioner's name, and the recital of the crimes and named entities carried from the petition. Every finding, the granting language, the date and the judge's signature are left blank because the judgment is the court's. No binary of CR370 is held by the repository or retained by Master Library Edition 1.1, so this component is authority-unmanifested and the track cannot reach packet_ready on it.

components.conditionDescription: Generated where the agency defendant list or the offense table exceeds the space on the form. CR360 twice directs the petitioner to attach additional sheets as necessary.
components.notes: Continuation sheets in the form's own layout, one for additional agency defendants and one for additional offenses, captioned to match the petition. This is not cosmetic: a participant with several cases or a long agency list will exceed the form, and an omitted agency is the single most common way a Missouri expungement half-works.

components.conditionDescription: Generated only where the participant answers that they cannot pay the filing fee and court costs.
components.notes: Motion and Affidavit in Support of Request to Proceed As a Poor Person, SJRC (07-15) GN10, under Rule 77.03 and § 514.040. The generic statewide revision is used; the Jackson-County-captioned copy in the corpus is a local variant and is never generated statewide. The court and county are data fields taken from the petition caption. The order to proceed as a poor person on page two is the court's and is left blank. The participant's household income, expenses, assets, debts and Social Security number are their own answers and the affidavit is sworn under penalty of perjury by them. The 07-15 revision is eleven years old and its currentness is unconfirmed, which is a release gate on this component rather than a reason to omit the fee-waiver route.

Sequenced participant instructions. Before filing: pull Case.net for every county and name variant; obtain the certified docket sheet, judgment and final disposition for each case; obtain the probation or parole discharge document; gather receipts for fines and restitution; and pull the Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based where the participant needs to see what is already closed under § 610.105. Then the filing: confirm the filing fee, copy count and any local cover sheet with the clerk of the court of charge, file the petition with FI-05 and the fee or GN10, and keep a file-stamped copy. Then what happens next: the clerk notices the prosecuting attorney, who has thirty days after receipt of service to object in writing; if an objection is filed the court holds a hearing within sixty days; if none is filed the court may still set a hearing and notice the named entities; a victim may be heard; and the court must issue an order of expungement or of dismissal within six months of filing. After the order: each named entity closes its record, court records become confidential and available only to the parties or by court order for good cause, and the central repository requests the Federal Bureau of Investigation to expunge its files. The instructions carry the refiling bar, the mandatory disclosure list, the prior-offense-at-sentencing rule and the agency-completeness warning above the signature block, and they say plainly that the former $250 surcharge under § 488.650 was repealed effective 28 August 2023 and must not be quoted.

tracks._participantInputsNote: What LegalEase asks. The exclusion analysis and the lifetime-cap count are the two answers that decide whether this track is even the right one, and both are participant-reported and attorney-gated rather than determined here.

participantInputs.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name a Missouri case was filed under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What is your driver licence number, the state that issued it, and its expiry date?
CR360 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.

List every Missouri case you want expunged: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county or municipality where it was charged, and a description of the charge. Every crime you want expunged has to be in this one petition.
Were all of the cases you listed charged, or the finding of guilt entered, in the same Missouri county? If they were in different counties, one petition cannot reach them all.
For each case, was the offense a felony, a misdemeanor, a municipal or ordinance violation, or an infraction?

For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date.
Have you paid every fine, court cost and restitution order in full on each of those cases?
Since the date you finished each case, have you been found guilty of any other misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any criminal charges pending right now, anywhere?

Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number, and say whether each was a felony, a misdemeanor or an ordinance violation with a possible jail term, or an infraction.

Were any of the cases you listed part of the same course of criminal conduct, or charged as counts in the same indictment or information? If so they can go in one petition and count only once, at the highest offense level.

Is any case on your list a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense that required sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an aircraft intoxication offense, an ordinance violation equivalent to any of those, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?

Which agencies do you believe hold records of these cases? Work from your own paperwork: the circuit court division, any municipal division, the county sheriff's department, the municipal police department, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney for each county, the Missouri Department of Revenue, and anyone else. Add every agency whose name appears on any document you have.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Case.net printouts, your court paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?

The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Missouri Supreme Court Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential and the number is not published through Case.net. What is it?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

Is any case on your list a conviction for possession of a controlled substance or for unlawful use or possession of drug paraphernalia? From 1 January 2027 at the latest, Missouri will expunge some of those automatically and free of charge, and an automatic expungement uses up the same lifetime slots as this petition.

tracks._supportingDocumentsNote: What the participant obtains and attaches. None of it delays generation: the packet is produced from the participant's answers and these are named as things to obtain before filing.

supportingDocuments.name: Case.net printout for each case
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: Case.net, the Missouri Judiciary's public case management system
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Search Case.net by your name, and by every name variant and spelling you have used, for every county you have lived in or been charged in. Print the case summary and the docket for each matter. Case.net does not show every municipal division, so it is a starting point rather than a complete record.

supportingDocuments.name: Certified docket sheet and judgment for each case
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where each case was charged or the finding of guilt entered
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of each court for a certified copy of the docket sheet and the judgment or final disposition. A per-page or per-document fee usually applies. This is the document that proves the case number, the court, the offense description and the disposition date.

supportingDocuments.name: Probation or parole discharge document
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Corrections, Division of Probation and Parole, or the supervising court
supportingDocuments.conditionDescription: Where the disposition included probation or parole.
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Ask your former probation or parole officer, or the Division of Probation and Parole, for the discharge document showing the date supervision ended. The waiting period runs from the day you completed the authorized disposition, and for a supervised case that is usually this date.

supportingDocuments.name: Receipts or a clerk's payment history for fines, costs and restitution
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the sentencing court
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the payment history on each case, showing a zero balance. Paragraph 3 of CR360 has you swear that all obligations relating to the disposition are satisfied, including fines and restitution, and an unpaid balance is a common and avoidable reason a petition is dismissed.

supportingDocuments.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Request your own criminal record through MACHS. A name-based search shows open records; a fingerprint-based search is the only way to see records that are already closed, including anything already closed by law under § 610.105. Confirm the current fees with the Patrol before ordering, and note that fingerprint capture carries a separate vendor service fee.

supportingDocuments.name: Missouri Department of Revenue driver record
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: Missouri Department of Revenue
supportingDocuments.conditionDescription: Where any case involves a traffic offense, an alcohol-related matter, or a commercial driver licence question.
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Order your Missouri driver record from the Department of Revenue. It shows administrative actions the court file will not, and it is the record that tells you whether a commercial driver licence issue is in play — which is an outright exclusion under § 610.140.3(10).

tracks._manualCompletionNote: What the packet deliberately leaves blank. Two of these are the sworn conclusions Missouri makes the petitioner's own, and one is the agency list the participant must verify rather than accept.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 5 — that the petitioner's habits and conduct demonstrate they are not a threat to the public safety of the state
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 2, numbered paragraph 5
manualCompletionItems.why: It is a conclusion about the participant, sworn under penalty of perjury, and § 610.140.6(5) makes it one of the two criteria that create the rebuttable presumption. LegalEase prompts for the participant's own facts and never asserts the conclusion. The review lists it first among the statements LegalEase must not generate on any Missouri track.

manualCompletionItems.item: Sworn paragraph 7 — that the expungement is consistent with the public welfare and the interests of justice warrant it
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 2, numbered paragraph 7
manualCompletionItems.why: The same reason. § 610.140.6(6) makes it the second presumption criterion, and it is a legal conclusion about the public interest rather than a fact about the participant.

manualCompletionItems.item: Paragraph 6's prior-expungement selection and the court and case number of any prior expungement
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 2, numbered paragraph 6
manualCompletionItems.why: Whether prior expungements have exhausted the § 610.140.13 caps is a legal judgment the review lists among the questions requiring individualized legal judgment. LegalEase asks for the participant's history, records their answer, and does not decide whether the caps remain available.

manualCompletionItems.item: Final verification of the defendant agency list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 1, defendant selections and the Other lines
manualCompletionItems.why: § 610.140.8 and the CR360 text both say the court's order of expungement shall not affect any person or entity not named as a defendant. A named agency closes its record; an unnamed agency keeps its copy, and the participant usually discovers that only when a later background check comes back. LegalEase builds the best list it can from the participant's own records because doing it badly is the most common way Missouri relief half-works, but the list is an assertion under oath about where records exist and the participant confirms it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The case number in the caption
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360, FI-05, CR370 and GN10 captions
manualCompletionItems.why: The clerk assigns it when the petition is filed.

manualCompletionItems.item: The petitioner's signature and the date
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR360 page 2, below the declaration under penalty of perjury
manualCompletionItems.why: The declaration is the participant's own sworn statement. LegalEase never signs it.

manualCompletionItems.item: The judge's findings, granting language, date and signature
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: CR370, Judgment and Order of Expungement
manualCompletionItems.why: The judgment is the court's. LegalEase supplies the caption and the recital of what was requested, nothing more.

manualCompletionItems.item: The hearing date, time, division and courtroom
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Participant instructions
manualCompletionItems.why: The court sets a hearing only after the objection window, and supplies the details. The packet is generated long before they exist.

manualCompletionItems.item: Any statement that a particular offense is or is not on the § 610.140.3 exclusion list
manualCompletionItems.whereInPacket: Not present in the packet at all
manualCompletionItems.why: Several exclusions turn on classification rather than on the offense name — whether a felony is a dangerous felony under § 556.061, whether an ordinance violation is substantially equivalent to an excluded offense, whether a § 571.030 weapons offense falls in a statutory exception. The review makes never auto-screening the eleven categories from self-report an express limitation, and it is a self-help boundary.

rules.filing: A petition filed with the clerk of the Missouri municipal, associate circuit or circuit court in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty (§ 610.140.2(1)). Rule 155.01 commences the action by filing a petition in the circuit court of the county in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty. Every crime sought to be expunged must be in the one petition (§ 610.140.2(2)). FI-05 is filed with it. Whether any circuit rejects the statewide CR360 in favour of a local form is unresolved, which is why the track carries a local-form override and a clerk-contact step.
rules.fees: Standard circuit court filing fees and costs apply, and they vary by county. Rule 155.02 governs filing fees and costs for an expungement action. The former $250 expungement surcharge under § 488.650 was repealed effective 28 August 2023 and must never be quoted. The exact current amount is county-variable and is confirmed with the clerk; costs may also include service, copying, certification and record-retrieval charges. The participant separately pays for the Highway Patrol record and for certified copies.
rules.feeWaiver: Motion and Affidavit in Support of Request to Proceed As a Poor Person, SJRC (07-15) GN10, under Rule 77.03 and § 514.040. The statewide revision is used, never the Jackson County variant in the corpus. The order granting leave to proceed as a poor person is on page two of the form and is the court's to sign.
rules.notice: The clerk of the court gives notice of the filing to the office of the prosecuting attorney that prosecuted the crimes listed (§ 610.140.6). The petitioner does not serve the prosecutor. If no objection is filed within thirty days after receipt of service the court may still set a hearing and must give reasonable notice to each entity named in the petition. A victim of a listed crime has an opportunity to be heard at any hearing.
rules.service: None performed by the participant. Notice is the clerk's function under § 610.140.6, and CR360 carries no certificate of service for the petitioner to complete. Rule 155.03 governs service in an expungement action.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs CR360 beneath the declaration required by § 610.140.14: I declare under penalty of perjury that the statements made herein are true and correct to the best of my knowledge, information, and belief. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank. The GN10 affidavit is separately sworn by the participant.
rules.notarization: none. CR360 uses a declaration under penalty of perjury rather than a notarial acknowledgment. This is the opposite of CR145 on the § 610.122 track, which must be subscribed and sworn before a notary, judge or clerk, and the two must not be conflated in participant copy.

selfHelpStopConditions: Any case that may fall in one of the eleven § 610.140.3 exclusion categories, including any felony assault, domestic assault, kidnapping, sex, weapons, child or death-related offense.
Any sex-offender registration issue, current or historic.
Any intoxication-related traffic, boating or aircraft offense, which is excluded here and belongs on the § 610.130 route if anywhere.
Any commercial driver licence or commercial motor vehicle involvement.
Any § 571.030 unlawful use of weapons offense, including where a statutory exception may apply.
Any question whether the § 610.140.13 lifetime caps remain available, or whether an automatic § 610.141 expungement has already consumed one.
Any question whether separate cases were part of the same course of criminal conduct.
Cases charged in more than one Missouri county, which one petition cannot reach.
Any uncertainty about the exact date the authorized disposition was completed.
The prosecuting attorney files a written objection, or a victim appears or asks to be heard.
The court sets a contested hearing.
A previous petition was dismissed, which bars refiling until a year has passed since the date that petition was filed.
The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence.
The participant asks about firearm rights, professional licensing, foster care or adoption, banking, insurance, gaming or federal employment.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: This is a single court packet on the current statewide form, not a staged or hybrid process. The review proposed four stages, and three of them are not legal units: the exclusion screen and cap count are eligibility questions and self-help boundaries, record retrieval is a participant filing requirement that never delays generation, and the prosecutor notice, objection window and hearing are the ordinary post-filing course of a § 610.140 petition that the clerk and the court run. What is left is one petition, one court, one filing and one legal effect, and § 610.140.14 requires the court to make the form available for pro se petitioners, which is what CR360 is. The output strategy is therefore official_pdf_fill on SJRC (10-24) CR360 with FI-05 at case type X5, CR370 as the conditional companion judgment, continuation sheets where the agency or offense lists overrun, and GN10 where the participant cannot pay. The obsolete OSCA (11-17) CR360 is never generated: its sworn paragraph 1 recites the superseded seven-year and three-year periods and would tell a participant to wait four years longer than the law requires. The two sworn conclusions in paragraphs 5 and 7, the prior-expungement disclosure in paragraph 6 and the final verification of the agency defendant list stay with the participant, because Missouri makes the completeness of that list decide how much relief the participant actually gets and makes a wrong answer bar refiling for a year.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge Records Related to an Arrest for an Eligible Crime (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.140.7)
tracks.publicName: An arrest that never became a charge

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 610.140.7 is a distinct petition inside the general expungement section and it was read verbatim from the Revisor's current text. It provides that a petition to expunge records related to an arrest for an eligible crime may be made in accordance with the provisions of the section to a court of competent jurisdiction in the county where the petitioner was arrested no earlier than eighteen months from the date of arrest, provided that during that time the petitioner has not been charged and has not been found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense. Two things follow and both were disputed in the retained review. The waiting period is eighteen months, not three years: the internal LegalEase reference was correct and the secondary source quoting three years was quoting a superseded version. And venue is the county of arrest, which differs from the court-of-charge rule that governs the conviction route. The eleven exclusion categories in § 610.140.3 apply unchanged, because the arrest must be for an eligible crime. Relief is mandatory under § 610.140.8 once the criteria are met, the clerk's notice, the thirty-day objection window, the sixty-day hearing rule and the six-month decision deadline all apply, and the effect is closure under § 610.120. This route is not § 610.122: that is a narrower false-information or qualifying-moving-violation mechanism with a different court, a different division, a fingerprint card, notarization and destruction rather than closure.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK 2 - Arrest-only expungement under § 610.140
provenance.sourceStatement: Controlling statute: § 610.140 RSMo, arrest-petition provision.

exclusions: Class A felonies (§ 610.140.3(1)).
Dangerous felonies as defined in § 556.061 (§ 610.140.3(2)).
Any offense requiring registration as a sex offender (§ 610.140.3(3)).
Any felony offense where death is an element of the offense (§ 610.140.3(4)).
Felony assault offenses, misdemeanor or felony domestic assault offenses, and felony kidnapping (§ 610.140.3(5)).
The specifically enumerated chapter 566 sex offenses and the listed offenses in other chapters (§ 610.140.3(6)).
Offenses eligible under § 610.130, so the first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense occupies its own lane and never routes here (§ 610.140.3(7)).
Intoxication-related traffic offenses and intoxication-related boating offenses, and operating an aircraft with an excessive blood alcohol content or while intoxicated (§ 610.140.3(8)).
Any ordinance violation substantially equivalent to an excluded offense (§ 610.140.3(9)).
Any offense of a motor vehicle law or ordinance committed by a person holding, or required to hold, a commercial driver's license (§ 610.140.3(10)).
Most unlawful use of weapons offenses under § 571.030, subject to the specific statutory exceptions (§ 610.140.3(11)).
Any arrest where the petitioner was charged during the eighteen months following the arrest. § 610.140.7 requires that the petitioner has not been charged during that time.
Any arrest where the petitioner was found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense during the eighteen months following the arrest.
An arrest that became a charge and then a conviction, plea or finding of guilt, which runs on mo-610-140-conviction instead.

An arrest based on false information, or an arrest for a chapter 303 misdemeanor or qualifying moving violation that was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, where the participant seeks destruction rather than closure. Those belong on mo-610-122-arrest-expungement, which is a different statute, court and division and a materially stronger remedy.

waitingPeriods.duration: Eighteen months from the date of arrest. Read verbatim from the current text: the petition may be made no earlier than eighteen months from the date of arrest. The three-year figure circulating in secondary sources is a superseded version and must not be used.
The same eighteen months. During that time the petitioner must not have been charged and must not have been found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense.

geography.venue: A court of competent jurisdiction in the county where the petitioner was arrested (§ 610.140.7). This is the arrest county, and it is deliberately different from the conviction route's court-of-charge rule. Where the participant was arrested in one county and any charge would have been filed in another, the arrest county controls this petition.

destination.name: Clerk of the circuit court in the Missouri county where the arrest occurred
destination.detail: Filed with the clerk of a court of competent jurisdiction in the county of arrest. The clerk assigns the case number, notices the prosecuting attorney under § 610.140.6, and distributes the order under § 610.140.8. Local practice and fees are confirmed with that clerk.

components.notes: The same statewide form as the conviction route — the Office of the State Courts Administrator publishes one § 610.140 petition, not two — completed with the arrest-only allegations and the arrest-county caption. This creates a real drafting problem the packet must solve rather than ignore: CR360's body text says all of the convictions listed below occurred and were prosecuted within the state of Missouri and I am filing this petition in the county where the conviction(s) was charged or I was found guilty, and its sworn paragraph 1 is written around completion of an authorized disposition. Neither sentence fits an arrest that never became a charge. The request line does reach an arrest — it asks the court to expunge the record of arrest, plea, trial, or conviction(s) — and the offense table accepts an arrest entry, so the form is usable, but the arrest-only allegations of § 610.140.7 are supplied on the attached continuation rather than by overwriting the form's printed text.

A required continuation page on this route rather than a conditional one, captioned to match the petition and carrying the § 610.140.7 allegations the printed form does not: that the petition concerns an arrest for an eligible crime and no charge was filed; the date of the arrest and the arresting agency; that at least eighteen months have passed since that date; that during those eighteen months the petitioner has not been charged and has not been found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense; and that the petition is filed in the county where the arrest occurred. It recites § 610.140.7 by subsection so a clerk or judge reading the file can see immediately which route is being used.

Case type code X5, Expungement of Records (610.140 RSMo). The code follows the statute rather than the word arrest: the Case Types List's separate XG code is captioned Expungement of Crim/Arrest Record and belongs to the § 610.122 route, and using it here would file a § 610.140 petition under the wrong case type. Full Social Security number under Operating Rule 4.07, as on the conviction route.

Findings, granting language, date and the judge's signature are left blank. The binary is not held by the repository and is not retained by Master Library Edition 1.1.

Sequenced participant instructions built around the two facts that differ from the conviction route. First, the eighteen-month clock runs from the date of arrest, so the participant needs the arrest date from the arresting agency's report or their Highway Patrol record rather than from a court file that may not exist. Second, the petition goes to the county of arrest, which may not be where the participant expected. The instructions then explain that they must be able to say no charge was ever filed — an arrest that became a charge is a different route entirely — and walk through the clerk's notice to the prosecutor, the thirty-day objection window, the sixty-day hearing rule and the six-month decision deadline. The closure warning is the same as the conviction route: the record is closed under § 610.120, not destroyed, and the packet must not use destruction language here.

tracks._participantInputsNote: What LegalEase asks. The single most consequential question is whether a charge was ever filed, because the answer decides between this route, the conviction route and the § 610.122 route.

participantInputs.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name you may have been arrested under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What is your driver licence number, the state that issued it, and its expiry date?
CR360 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.
On what date were you arrested? The eighteen-month waiting period runs from this date.
In which Missouri county were you arrested? If the arrest happened inside a municipality, name the municipality too. This petition is filed in the county of arrest.
Which agency arrested you?
What offense were you arrested for, as it appears on the arrest paperwork or on your Highway Patrol record?

Were you ever formally charged in court for this arrest — an information, an indictment, a complaint, a summons or a ticket that opened a court case? If a case was opened, this is not the right route.
Since the date of that arrest, have you been charged with any other criminal offense?
Since the date of that arrest, have you been found guilty of any misdemeanor or felony offense?

Was the offense you were arrested for a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense requiring sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an equivalent ordinance violation, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?

Was your arrest based on false information, or was it for a chapter 303 misdemeanor or a moving violation that was later dismissed, nolle prossed or ended in a not-guilty finding? If so there is a stronger Missouri route under § 610.122 that destroys the record rather than closing it, and you should look at that first.

Which agencies do you believe hold records of this arrest? Start with the arresting agency, the county sheriff's department, any municipal police department, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney for the county, the court, and the Missouri Department of Revenue.
The court's order will not affect any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Highway Patrol record and your arrest paperwork and confirmed this list is complete?
Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number and the offense level.
The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential. What is it?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

rules.filing: A petition filed with the clerk of a court of competent jurisdiction in the county where the petitioner was arrested (§ 610.140.7), no earlier than eighteen months from the date of arrest. FI-05 is filed with it. Rules 155.01 to 155.05 govern commencement, fees, service, notice and hearing, and judgment.
rules.fees: Standard circuit court filing fees and costs, county-variable, confirmed with the clerk. The repealed § 488.650 surcharge is never quoted.
rules.feeWaiver: GN10 under Rule 77.03 and § 514.040, statewide revision, generated only on request.
rules.notice: The clerk gives notice of the filing to the prosecuting attorney (§ 610.140.6). Written objection is due within thirty days after receipt of service; a hearing follows within sixty days of any objection unless the parties agree otherwise; where no objection is filed the court may still set a hearing and must notice each entity named in the petition.
rules.service: None performed by the participant. Notice is the clerk's function.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner signs CR360 beneath the § 610.140.14 declaration under penalty of perjury, and separately signs the continuation carrying the § 610.140.7 allegations. LegalEase leaves both blank.
rules.notarization: none. A declaration under penalty of perjury is used, not a notarial acknowledgment.

unresolvedQuestions.question: How an arrest-only § 610.140.7 petition should be presented on CR360, whose printed body text is written for convictions. The form says all of the convictions listed below occurred and were prosecuted within the state of Missouri and that the petition is filed in the county where the conviction was charged or the petitioner found guilty, both of which are wrong for an arrest with no charge filed in the arrest county. The Office of the State Courts Administrator publishes no separate arrest-only § 610.140 form. The packet supplies the § 610.140.7 allegations on a required continuation rather than altering the form's printed text, which is the fail-closed reading, but whether Missouri clerks accept that presentation is unconfirmed.

tracks.legalName: Closure of Official Records on Nolle Prosequi, Dismissal, Acquittal or Suspended Imposition of Sentence (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.105)
tracks.publicName: Cases that already closed by law

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 610.105 was read in full from the Revisor's current text, effective 28 August 2006, and it is short. Subsection 1 provides that where the imposition of sentence is suspended in the court in which the case originated, or where a case is nolle prossed, dismissed, or the accused is found not guilty, official records pertaining to the case shall thereafter be closed records when the case is finally terminated, except as provided in subsection 2 and in § 610.120, save that the judgment or order of the court remains a public record. Where a not-guilty finding rests on mental disease or defect excluding responsibility under § 552.030, the records close upon that finding and access is limited to law enforcement, child-care agencies, facilities defined in § 198.006 and in-home services providers defined in § 192.2400. Subsection 2 supplies the section's only exception: where the charge is a chapter 566 offense or one of the enumerated offenses in §§ 568.045, 568.050, 568.060, 568.065, 568.175 or 573.200 and 573.205, and the imposition of sentence was suspended, the records shall be made available to the victim for use in the victim's own judicial proceeding, and a minor victim's parent or guardian may request them on the victim's behalf. Nothing in the section contemplates a petition, motion, application, request or filing of any kind by the person whose records close. Closure happens by operation of law on final termination, which for a suspended imposition of sentence means completion of probation. The review's enumeration of the statutory exceptions was left undone on its pass; there is exactly one, and it is a victim-access exception rather than a category of case that fails to close.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK 3 - Automatic closure of terminated cases
provenance.sourceStatement: Controlling statute: § 610.105 RSMo.

exclusions: Any case that has not been finally terminated. For a suspended imposition of sentence that means probation is still running; closure does not occur until it ends.
A conviction, a guilty plea followed by a suspended execution of sentence, or any disposition other than the four in § 610.105.1. Those close only through a § 610.140 petition, if at all.
The judgment or order of the court itself, which § 610.105.1 expressly keeps a public record even after the rest of the file closes.

Not an exception to closure but a limit on it: under § 610.105.2, where the charge was a chapter 566 offense or one of the enumerated offenses in §§ 568.045, 568.050, 568.060, 568.065, 568.175, 573.200 or 573.205 and imposition of sentence was suspended, the records are made available to the victim for use in the victim's own judicial proceeding.
The access § 610.120 preserves for law enforcement, courts, and the other entities that section names. Closure is not invisibility.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Closure operates on final termination of the case. For a nolle prosequi, dismissal or not-guilty finding that is the disposition itself; for a suspended imposition of sentence it is completion of the probation term.

geography.venue: None. Closure operates by law in the court in which the case originated and at the central repository; there is no filing, so there is no venue. Where the participant needs to verify closure they deal with the clerk of the originating court and with the Missouri State Highway Patrol, neither of which is a filing destination.

destination.name: No participant filing destination — closure by operation of law
destination.detail: Nothing is filed and nothing is submitted. § 610.105 closes the records on final termination without any act by the person whose records they are. The participant's only dealings are informational: a Case.net search, a request to the clerk of the originating court for the docket, and a fingerprint-based criminal record request to the Missouri State Highway Patrol, which is the only search that shows records already closed.

components.notes: The whole of the output on this track, and it is verification rather than a filing. Step one, confirm the disposition really is a nolle prosequi, a dismissal, a not-guilty finding or a suspended imposition of sentence, working from the certified docket rather than from memory — a suspended execution of sentence is a conviction and is not on this route. Step two, confirm final termination, which for a suspended imposition of sentence means probation has ended. Step three, check whether the case still appears publicly on Case.net. Step four, order a fingerprint-based Highway Patrol record, which is the only way to see what is already closed. Step five, if the record is still public, that is where self-help ends: whether closure failed or whether closure simply does not reach that particular record is a legal question, not a form. Step six, if closure did occur, explain plainly what it means — the file is closed, the judgment or order remains a public record, § 610.120 preserves access for the entities it names, and a victim may reach a § 610.105.2 file. And step seven, explain the difference between closure and expungement, because a participant with a closed case may still benefit from a § 610.140 petition and should not be told the two are the same thing.

components.conditionDescription: Included where the participant reports that a case appearing to qualify under § 610.105 is still showing publicly on Case.net, on a background check, or on their Highway Patrol record.
components.notes: The discrepancy pathway, and it is deliberately a referral rather than a document. Missouri publishes no participant-facing record-correction petition, motion or application for a § 610.105 closure that did not take effect: the section creates no such remedy, and the Highway Patrol's own challenge process under its criminal-record review procedures runs through the Patrol and back to the reporting agency rather than through any court filing. So the guidance names the three places a stale record lives — the court file, the central repository, and a private background-check vendor's database, which is a fourth problem the court cannot fix — tells the participant which of the three they are actually looking at, and routes them to legal aid or counsel. It does not invent a correction petition.

participantInputs.question: How did the case end? Was it dismissed, was it nolle prossed by the prosecutor, were you found not guilty, or did the judge suspend the imposition of sentence and put you on probation?

participantInputs.question: Was it a suspended imposition of sentence, or a suspended execution of sentence? They sound alike and the difference decides everything: a suspended imposition closes automatically, a suspended execution is a conviction and does not.

When you search Case.net for your name, does this case still come up?
Does this case appear on the criminal record you obtained from the Missouri State Highway Patrol?
Has this case appeared on a background check run by an employer, a landlord or a licensing body? If so, who ran it and when?

Was the charge a chapter 566 sex offense, or one of the offenses in §§ 568.045, 568.050, 568.060, 568.065, 568.175, 573.200 or 573.205, with the imposition of sentence suspended? If so, the law lets the victim of that offense obtain the closed records for use in their own case.

Closure and expungement are different. A closed case can still be reached by the entities § 610.120 names, and the judgment stays public. Would you like to know whether a § 610.140 expungement petition would give you more than closure already has?

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Guidance is the correct output and the ground is precise rather than conclusory: § 610.105 closes the records by operation of law on final termination and creates no petition, motion, application, request or filing of any kind for the person whose records they are. There is nothing to generate because there is nothing to file, which is the one rationale that keeps a track off the guidance re-review queue. The re-review the mission required was run and it changed nothing: Missouri publishes no participant-facing correction petition for a closure that did not take effect, the Highway Patrol's record-review challenge runs through the Patrol and back to the reporting agency rather than through any court, and inventing a correction petition would put a document into the world that Missouri law does not authorise. The guidance is therefore verification and classification — confirm the disposition, confirm final termination, check Case.net, check the fingerprint-based Highway Patrol record, and explain the difference between closure and expungement — with a referral where the record is still public. Generating a § 610.140 petition for a case that is already closed wastes the participant's filing fee and one of their lifetime cap slots, so the check runs before any petition is offered.

limitations.statement: Closure is not expungement and the guidance must keep them apart. A closed § 610.105 record leaves the judgment or order a public record, preserves the access § 610.120 grants, and may be reached by a victim under § 610.105.2. A § 610.140 order does more. Telling a participant their case is closed is not telling them it is gone.

tracks.legalName: Verified Petition for Expungement of Arrest Records (Mo. Rev. Stat. §§ 610.122, 610.123 and 610.124)
tracks.publicName: An arrest based on false information

controllingAuthority.summary: Sections 610.122, 610.123 and 610.124 were read in full from the Revisor's current text and together they are the strongest record-clearing remedy Missouri has. § 610.122, effective 28 August 2021, allows any record of arrest recorded under § 43.503 to be expunged on either of two alternative grounds. The first is that the court determines the arrest was based on false information and that there is no probable cause at the time of the action to expunge to believe the individual committed the offense, no charges will be pursued as a result of the arrest, and the subject did not receive a suspended imposition of sentence for the offense of arrest or any related offense. The second is that the court determines the person was arrested for, or subsequently charged with, a misdemeanor offense of chapter 303 or any moving violation as defined in § 302.010 other than an intoxication-related traffic offense as defined in § 577.023, that each offense or violation related to the arrest was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, and that the person is not a commercial driver's licence holder and was not operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the arrest. § 610.122.2 adds that a record is eligible only if no civil action is pending relating to the arrest or the records sought to be expunged. § 610.123 supplies the procedure and it is unusually specific: a verified petition filed in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest, which shall be dismissed if it does not contain the petitioner's full name, sex, race, date of birth, driver's licence number, Social Security number and address at the time of arrest, the offense charged, the date of arrest, the county and any municipality of arrest, the arresting agency, the case number and court, and the petitioner's fingerprints on a standard fingerprint card at the time of filing, forwarded to the central repository for the sole purpose of positively identifying the petitioner. The petition names as defendants all law enforcement agencies, courts, prosecuting attorneys, central state depositories and others the petitioner has reason to believe may possess the records, and the court's order does not affect any person or entity not named. The court sets a hearing no sooner than thirty days from filing and gives reasonable notice to each named entity. § 610.123.4 makes relief mandatory on the findings — if the court finds the petitioner is entitled to expungement of any record that is the subject of the petition, it shall enter an order directing expungement — which closes an open question the review could not answer. § 610.124 then requires that all records ordered expunged be destroyed, or blacked out where destruction is not feasible because of the permanent nature of the record books, removed from all electronic files maintained with the State of Missouri, and that the central repository request the Federal Bureau of Investigation to expunge the records from its files. § 610.124.2 gives any petitioner, or agency protesting the expungement, the ordinary civil right of appeal. This is the one Missouri track where the word destroyed is accurate.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK 4 - False-information and qualifying moving-violation arrest expungement
provenance.sourceStatement: Controlling statute: §§ 610.122, 610.123, and 610.124 RSMo.

exclusions: Any arrest where the subject received a suspended imposition of sentence for the offense of arrest or for any offense related to the arrest (§ 610.122.1(1)(c)). This bars the false-information ground outright.

Any record where a civil action is pending relating to the arrest or to the records sought to be expunged (§ 610.122.2). This is a bar on both grounds and it reaches civil actions the participant may not think of as related.

On the moving-violation ground, any intoxication-related traffic offense or intoxication-related boating offense as defined under § 577.001. Those are excluded expressly and belong on the § 610.130 route if anywhere.
On the moving-violation ground, any person who is a commercial driver's licence holder or who was operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the arrest (§ 610.122.1(2)(b)).
On the moving-violation ground, any offense or violation related to the arrest that was not nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted. Every related offense must have ended that way.
An offense that is neither a chapter 303 misdemeanor nor a moving violation as defined in § 302.010, where the participant is relying on the moving-violation ground rather than on false information.
An arrest that resulted in a conviction, which is not reachable under § 610.122 on either ground and runs on § 610.140 instead.

waitingPeriods.duration: none. Neither § 610.122 nor § 610.123 states a waiting period, and none is implied. What the false-information ground requires instead is a present-tense finding — that there is no probable cause at the time of the action to expunge — so the question is the state of the evidence now rather than the passage of time.

geography.venue: The civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest (§ 610.123.1). Both the court and the division differ from the § 610.140 routes: this is a civil action, not a criminal-side petition, and it is fixed to the arrest county rather than to the court of charge. Where the arrest occurred in a municipality the municipality is named in the petition but the filing is still in the circuit court's civil division for that county.

destination.name: Civil division of the Missouri circuit court in the county of arrest
destination.detail: Filed with the clerk of the circuit court, civil division, for the county where the arrest occurred. The clerk then does three things the printed instructions on CR145 set out: issues a copy of the petition to the prosecuting attorney; sends a copy of the petition and the fingerprint card to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository at the Highway Patrol; and gives notice of the hearing to the prosecuting attorney and to each official, agency or other entity named in the petition. The court sets the hearing no sooner than thirty days from filing.

components.notes: The current statewide petition, SJRC (04-24) CR145, two pages and forty-eight AcroForm fields, superseding the OSCA (10-16) copy in the corpus. legalDesignDecision.rationale: One court packet on the current statewide form, not a staged process. The review proposed three stages and two of them are not legal units: ground selection is an eligibility question and a self-help boundary, and obtaining a fingerprint card is a physical prerequisite of filing that the adopted packet-only amendment expressly declines to treat as a generation gate. What remains is a single verified petition, filed once, in one court, producing one order. The output strategy is official_pdf_fill on SJRC (04-24) CR145 with FI-05 at case type XG, the fingerprint card as a required-before-filing attachment, the conditional CR143 judgment and the conditional GN10 fee waiver. Two of the review's open questions are closed from primary authority: § 610.123.4 makes relief mandatory on the findings — if the court finds the petitioner entitled, it shall enter an order directing expungement — and the fingerprint card comes from a local law enforcement agency rather than from a Highway Patrol record purchase, so the procedure is instructable even though the statewide cost is not published. The false-information ground remains an unconditional referral because it requires proving that someone else supplied false information, which is contested evidence rather than a form field, and the participant's own words are recited rather than drafted. This is the only Missouri track that may use destruction language, and it must, because § 610.124 says it.

tracks.legalName: Application for Expungement of a First Intoxication-Related Traffic or Boating Offense (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.130)
tracks.publicName: A first drink-driving or boating offense

citations: S.S. v. Mitchell, 289 S.W.3d 797 (Mo. App. E.D. 2009)
controllingAuthority.summary: Section 610.130 was read in full from the Revisor's current text. It was transferred from former § 577.054 in 2014 and has been effective in its present form since 1 January 2017. Subsection 1 allows an individual who has pleaded guilty to or been convicted of a first intoxication-related traffic offense or intoxication-related boating offense which is a misdemeanor or a county or city ordinance violation, and which is not a conviction for driving a commercial motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol, and who since that date has not been convicted of any intoxication-related traffic or boating offense, to apply after a period of not less than ten years to the court in which he or she pled guilty or was sentenced for an order expunging from all official records all recordations of the arrest, plea, trial or conviction. Subsection 2 makes relief mandatory: if the court determines, after hearing, that the person has not been convicted of any subsequent intoxication-related traffic or boating offense, has no other subsequent alcohol-related enforcement contacts as defined in § 302.525, and has no other such offense or alcohol-related enforcement action pending at the time of the hearing, the court shall enter an order of expungement. Subsection 3 makes the records confidential and available only to the parties or by order of the court for good cause shown, restores the person to the status occupied before the arrest, plea or conviction as if the event had never taken place, supplies a perjury shield, and limits a person to one expungement under the section, while allowing the director to keep records sufficient to enforce that limit. Subsection 4 excludes anyone who has been issued or is required to possess a commercial driver's licence in Missouri or any other state. The section stands entirely apart from § 610.140, which excludes offenses eligible under § 610.130 at subsection 3(7) and intoxication-related traffic and boating offenses generally at subsection 3(8), so the two never overlap and a drink-driving matter must never be routed through the general track. Two points the review left open are now answered. Alcohol-related enforcement contacts is not an open-textured phrase: § 302.525.3 defines it as any suspension or revocation under §§ 302.500 to 302.540, any suspension or revocation entered in Missouri or any other state for a refusal to submit to chemical testing under an implied consent law, and any conviction in Missouri or any other state for a violation involving driving while intoxicated, driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol, or driving a vehicle while having an unlawful alcohol concentration. And relief under this section reaches the administrative side: S.S. v. Mitchell holds that the section authorises a court to expunge the records of a driver's administrative alcohol suspension and to make those records confidential.

exclusions: Any person who has been issued a commercial driver's licence, or who is required to possess one, in Missouri or any other state (§ 610.130.4). This is a status bar, not an offense bar, and it is asked about current status as well as status at the time of the offense.
A conviction for driving a commercial motor vehicle while under the influence of alcohol (§ 610.130.1).
Any felony intoxication-related traffic or boating offense. The section reaches a misdemeanor or a county or city ordinance violation only.
Any person convicted of a subsequent intoxication-related traffic offense or intoxication-related boating offense since the first plea or conviction (§§ 610.130.1 and 2).

components.notes: An Application and Petition for Expungement under § 610.130, drafted by LegalEase against the statutory contents. The Office of the State Courts Administrator publishes no form for this section — confirmed twice over, from the 16th Judicial Circuit's own informational sheet, which says of the § 610.130 route that there are no forms provided, you or your attorney must draft and file all pleadings, and from a June 2024 Missouri pro se guide which lists § 610.130 among the statutes for which there are no Missouri court forms prepared and directs the reader to draft their own petition modelled on the published forms. The pleading follows the OSCA pattern the review describes: the standard Missouri caption naming the judicial circuit and county with the case number left blank; a respondent block naming every agency believed to hold records, including the court, the arresting agency, the prosecuting or city attorney, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division and the Missouri Department of Revenue; numbered allegations tracking each statutory condition in turn — that the offense was the applicant's first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense, that it was a misdemeanor or a county or city ordinance violation, that it was not a conviction for driving a commercial motor vehicle under the influence, the plea or sentencing date and the court, that not less than ten years have passed, that there has been no subsequent intoxication-related traffic or boating conviction, that there has been no other subsequent alcohol-related enforcement contact as defined in § 302.525, that no such offense or enforcement action is pending, that the applicant has never been issued and is not required to possess a commercial driver's licence in any state, and that the applicant has not previously received an expungement under this section; a prayer for an order expunging from all official records all recordations of the arrest, plea, trial and conviction and directing the named agencies to expunge their records; and a declaration under penalty of perjury. LegalEase drafts the structure and recites the applicant's own answers; it asserts none of the conclusions.

A proposed Order of Expungement on the same caption, drafted to § 610.130.2 and 3. It recites the findings the statute requires the court to make after hearing, orders expungement from all official records of all recordations of the arrest, plea, trial and conviction, directs each named agency to expunge its records, and records that the records maintained in any administrative or court proceeding become confidential and available only to the parties or by order of the court for good cause shown and that the applicant is restored to the status occupied before the arrest, plea or conviction. Findings language is drafted as proposed findings for the court to adopt or reject; the date and the judge's signature are left blank.

Sequenced participant instructions, and they carry more weight here than on any other Missouri track because the relief is once in a lifetime. Before filing: obtain the certified docket and judgment from the court of plea or sentence; obtain the Missouri Department of Revenue driver record, which is the document that shows administrative suspensions and revocations and is therefore the only practical way to see an alcohol-related enforcement contact that never produced a conviction; obtain the Highway Patrol criminal record; and check whether a commercial driver licence has ever been issued in any state. Then confirm with the clerk of the court of plea whether the application opens a new case or is filed under the original number, what the fee is, whether a cover sheet is required and which case type code to use, and whether that court has a local form. Then file the application and proposed order. The court holds a hearing and the participant attends. The instructions carry the once-in-a-lifetime warning above the signature block, in the same place the § 610.140 packet carries the refiling bar, and they state plainly that every intoxication-related matter is an attorney-review recommendation rather than a routine self-help filing.

participantInputs.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case may be under?
What is your date of birth?
What is your current mailing address?
What was the offense? Was it a drink- or drug-driving offense, or a boating offense?
Was it charged as a state misdemeanor, or as a county or city ordinance violation? A felony is not eligible under this section.
On what date did you plead guilty or were you sentenced? The ten-year period runs from then.
Which court took your plea or sentenced you — the municipal division, the associate circuit division, or the circuit court — and in which county? That is where this application is filed.
What was the case number?
Was this your first intoxication-related traffic or boating offense, anywhere? The section reaches a first offense only.
Since that plea or conviction, have you been convicted of any other drink- or drug-driving offense or intoxication-related boating offense, in Missouri or any other state?

Since then, has your driving licence been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it is the question people most often answer wrongly.
Do you have any drink- or drug-driving charge, boating offense, or licence suspension or revocation proceeding pending right now?

Have you ever been issued a commercial driver's licence, in Missouri or in any other state, or are you required to hold one for your work? This bars the whole section, whether or not it had anything to do with the offense.
Were you driving a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the offense?
Have you ever had an expungement under this section before? You are entitled to only one, ever, and it cannot be undone.

Which agencies do you believe hold records of this matter? Include the court, the arresting agency, the prosecuting or city attorney, the Missouri State Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division and the Missouri Department of Revenue.
Have you checked your driver record and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The review's build blocker was the strategy classification: custom pleading if no form exists, official form fill if one does. It is closed, and the answer is that no form exists. Two independent Missouri sources say so — the 16th Judicial Circuit's own informational sheet, which states of the § 610.130 route that there are no forms provided and the applicant or their attorney must draft and file all pleadings, and a June 2024 Missouri pro se guide, which lists § 610.130 among the statutes for which no Missouri court forms are prepared and tells the reader to draft their own petition modelled on the published forms. The output strategy is therefore custom_pleading with localFormOverride so that any circuit or municipal division publishing its own form governs there. The review's caution against drafting a § 610.130 petition before confirming no form exists was right and has been honoured; the confirmation is now on the record and the pleading may be built. The statute supplies everything a pleading needs: who may apply, the ten-year period, the conditions, the venue, the hearing, the mandatory grant on the findings, the relief and the order's effect. Two of the review's open questions are answered — alcohol-related enforcement contact is defined at § 302.525.3, and the section reaches administrative suspension records — and the definition is reproduced in the packet rather than paraphrased. The track keeps its attorney-review recommendation on its face: not because a hearing is required or because relief is discretionary, which it is not, but because the ten-year clean-record showing turns on a driver record most participants have never read and the relief is available exactly once.

tracks.legalName: Marijuana Expungement, Vacatur and Release from Supervision (Mo. Const. art. XIV, § 2)

controllingAuthority.summary: Article XIV, section 2 of the Missouri Constitution is constitutional rather than statutory, which matters because ordinary legislation cannot narrow it. Its expungement provisions were read from the Revisor's current constitutional text and they create three legally different situations rather than one. A person currently incarcerated in a prison, jail or halfway house for a marijuana-related offense that would not have been an offense, or would have been a lesser offense, under sections 1 and 2, or who is serving a sentence for a qualifying marijuana misdemeanor or a class E or class D felony involving three pounds or less, may petition the sentencing court to vacate the sentence, order immediate release or a change in supervision status, and expunge all government records of the case. A person on probation or parole for such an offense has the sentence automatically vacated and supervision terminated without any petition. A person who has completed the sentence is entitled to court-ordered expungement, and the courts were directed to process those cases on a schedule — ninety days for misdemeanor marijuana offenses, one hundred and eighty days for class E felonies and the remaining misdemeanors, and two hundred and seventy days for class D felonies involving three pounds or less and lesser offenses — with class A, B and C felonies expunged on completion of incarceration including any supervised probation or parole. Excluded throughout are offenses involving distribution or delivery to a minor, offenses involving violence, and offenses of operating a motor vehicle while under the influence of marijuana. The effect is the strongest in Missouri: the order is legally effective immediately, the conviction and sentence are vacated as legally invalid, the person is treated in all respects as if he or she had never been arrested, convicted or sentenced, and the court must issue a certificate stating that the offense has been expunged. The state public defender was directed to provide accessible pro se forms and circuit courts to make them readily available; the Office of the State Courts Administrator now publishes SJRC (10-24) CR375 for the purpose, which supersedes the unofficial modified public-defender form in the corpus.
