units.label: Court-ordered and automatic Article XIV relief — verification, no participant filing
units.description: The first branch, and it is a legally distinct mechanism rather than a preliminary check. Article XIV, section 2 directs the courts themselves to order expungement for people who have completed their sentences, on constitutional deadlines the courts were given, and automatically vacates the sentence and terminates supervision for a person on probation or parole without any petition at all. For both of those populations there is no participant filing, no application, no request and no form: the constitution puts the act on the court. CR375 confirms the design from the other direction — its two selectable postures are currently incarcerated and not currently incarcerated or on probation, so a participant presently on probation or parole for a marijuana offense fits neither box, because the constitution does not ask them to petition. The unit's output is therefore verification and explanation: identify the marijuana case and the sentencing county, check Case.net and the Highway Patrol record to see whether expungement was already ordered, and, where it was, help the participant ask the court for the certificate of expungement the constitution requires it to issue. Where relief was not entered the participant is routed to the second unit. What the unit must not do is promise that relief occurred: the constitution directed the courts to process these cases, and a direction is not a receipt.

units.label: CR375 petition to the sentencing court under Article XIV, section 2
units.description: The second branch: the participant's own petition on the current statewide form, SJRC (10-24) CR375, filed in the county where the conviction was charged or the finding of guilt entered. It is the required route for a person currently incarcerated for a qualifying marijuana offense, who the constitution says may petition the sentencing court to vacate the sentence, order immediate release or a change in supervision status, and expunge all government records. And it is the fallback for a person who has completed their sentence and for whom the court-directed relief in unit 1 did not happen, which is why the two units are alternatives rather than stages. LegalEase completes the caption, the defendant agency selections, the identity block and the case table, and recites the participant's selection of posture. The relief the form requests — vacatur of the sentence, immediate release from incarceration or other supervision, and expungement of the record of arrest, plea, trial and conviction — is the constitution's own language and is not softened. Where the participant is currently incarcerated or under supervision the packet is generated with a mandatory attorney handoff on its face, because a petition seeking immediate release is a liberty application and not a self-help filing.

geography.venue: For the petition branch, the county where the conviction was charged or the finding of guilt entered, which is what CR375 states on its face — the marijuana-related convictions listed below occurred and were prosecuted within the state of Missouri and I am filing this petition in the county where the conviction(s) was/were charged or I was found guilty. The review recorded venue as the county of the original sentencing court, taken from the unofficial public-defender form; the official form says court of charge or finding of guilt and the official form controls. For the incarcerated posture the constitution speaks of petitioning the sentencing court, and where the sentencing court and the court of charge differ the participant confirms with the clerk. For the verification branch there is no venue, because there is no filing.

destination.name: Clerk of the Missouri court where the marijuana conviction was charged or the finding of guilt entered
destination.detail: Unit 2 is filed with the clerk of that court, with FI-05 at case type X#. Unit 1 has no filing destination: the court acts of its own motion under the constitution for the completed-sentence population and the vacatur is automatic for the supervision population, and the participant's only dealings are a Case.net search, a Highway Patrol record request and a request to the clerk for the certificate of expungement where relief was already entered.

components.notes: Unit 2's petition: the current statewide Petition for Expungement — Marijuana-Related Offense(s), SJRC (10-24) CR375, two pages and seventy-seven AcroForm fields, retained by Master Library Edition 1.1 as a packet-form candidate. LegalEase completes the judicial circuit and county, the defendant agency selections — circuit court division, county sheriff's department, municipal police department, the Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division, the prosecuting or circuit attorney by county, and free-text Other lines — the identity block, and the case table of case number, court name, approximate date of charge, county of charge and the number and description of the charge. Note that CR375 asks for year of birth only, not a full date of birth, which is a deliberate privacy design on the form and is preserved rather than filled in with more than the form asks. The posture selection between currently incarcerated and not currently incarcerated or on probation is the participant's, and it is the field that routes them between the two units. The declaration under penalty of perjury and signature are left blank. The unofficial modified Missouri State Public Defender pro se form in the corpus is never generated: it carries no OSCA number, was modified by an unknown hand, and CR375 exists.

Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet at case type code X#, Expunge Marijuana Criminal/Arrest Records, read from the Case Types List's circuit column. This is the one Missouri case type code that names the relief unambiguously and there is no routing ambiguity about it. The full Social Security number is required under Operating Rule 4.07 and goes here; it does not go on CR375, which does not ask for it, and CR375's year-of-birth-only design means the confidential sheet is carrying materially more identifying data than the petition.

Unit 1 in full, and the filing and follow-up instructions for unit 2. The verification sequence comes first because filing where relief already exists wastes the participant's money: identify the marijuana case and the county where it was charged; search Case.net for the case and for your name; order a fingerprint-based Highway Patrol record, which is the only search that shows records already closed; and read what you find. If expungement was already ordered, the instruction is not to file anything but to ask the clerk of that court for the certificate of expungement, which Article XIV requires the court to issue and which is the document a participant actually needs to show an employer or a landlord. If it was not, and the offense qualifies, unit 2's petition follows. For unit 2 the instructions cover the posture selection, filing in the county of charge with FI-05 at case type X#, and the fact that the relief requested is immediate and constitutional: the order is legally effective immediately, the conviction and sentence are vacated as legally invalid, the participant is treated in all respects as if never arrested, convicted or sentenced, and a certificate of expungement is to be issued. Where the participant is incarcerated or under supervision, the instructions open with the attorney handoff rather than closing with it.

components.conditionDescription: Included where verification shows expungement was already ordered and the participant needs the certificate the constitution requires.
components.notes: The certificate-of-expungement request. Article XIV, section 2 requires the court to issue a certificate stating that the offense has been expunged, and it is the practical proof of relief. The Office of the State Courts Administrator publishes no numbered certificate form or certificate request form that could be located, so this is a guided request to the clerk of the court that entered the order rather than a generated document: the participant identifies the case and the order, asks for the certificate, and asks what the fee and turnaround are. If a numbered certificate form is later identified this component becomes an official form fill.

participantInputs.question: Right now, are you in prison, jail or a halfway house for this marijuana case; on probation or parole for it; or have you finished the sentence completely? Missouri treats those three situations differently under the constitution.
What is your full legal name, and any other name the case may be under?
What year were you born? CR375 asks only for the year, not the full date.
CR375 asks for your sex and for your race and ethnicity. How would you like those answered? You may choose more than one, or Unknown.
What is your current mailing address, or the address of the facility where you are held?
List each marijuana case: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county where it was charged, and the number and description of the charge.
In which Missouri county was each case charged, or the finding of guilt entered? That is where the petition is filed.
For each case, was the offense a misdemeanor, a class E felony, a class D felony, a class A, B or C felony, or a city or county ordinance violation?
For each case, how much marijuana was involved? Three pounds is the line for a class D felony.
Did any of these cases involve giving or selling marijuana to someone under 21, any violence, or driving while under the influence of marijuana? Any of those is outside this route.

Have you checked Case.net and your Highway Patrol record to see whether this case has already been expunged? Missouri courts were directed by the constitution to clear many of these cases without anyone asking, and filing for something you already have wastes your money.

If the case was already expunged, would you like help asking the court for the certificate of expungement? The constitution requires the court to issue one and it is the document you can show an employer.
participantInputs.conditionDescription: Asked where verification indicates expungement has already been ordered.

participantInputs.question: Which agencies do you believe hold records of these cases? Include the circuit court division, the county sheriff's department, any municipal police department, the Highway Patrol Criminal Justice Information Services Division and the prosecuting or circuit attorney for each county.
Have you checked your paperwork and your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?
The Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet requires your full Social Security number under Operating Rule 4.07. That sheet is confidential and is not published through Case.net. What is it?

Would what you did still be a crime today under Missouri's marijuana amendment, and if so would it be a lesser offense than what you were convicted of? This is the eligibility test and it is about current law, not about what the charge was called at the time.

tracks._limitationsNote: Counsel approved this track with limitations. The composition follows the constitution's three populations rather than a workflow.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: This is the one Missouri track where composition is right, and it is right for a statutory reason rather than a workflow one. Article XIV, section 2 creates legally distinct mechanisms for three populations: it directs the courts themselves to order expungement for people who have completed their sentences, on constitutional deadlines; it vacates the sentence and terminates supervision automatically for a person on probation or parole, without any petition; and it gives a person currently incarcerated the right to petition the sentencing court for vacatur, release and expungement. The first two involve no participant filing at all and the third is a petition on a statewide form, which is exactly the participant-filing-versus-automatic-relief pair that the composition rule contemplates. The mode is alternative rather than sequential because a participant belongs on one branch or the other, not on both in order: for the completed-sentence population unit 2 is the fallback where the court did not act, and for the incarcerated population unit 2 is the only route. CR375 corroborates the structure from the form side, since its two selectable postures leave the supervision population with no box to tick. This is not ordinary record checking dressed up as a unit — the constitution puts the act on the court, and generating a petition for someone whose relief the court was constitutionally obliged to enter is both wasteful and wrong. Unit 2 is official_pdf_fill on SJRC (10-24) CR375 with FI-05 at case type X#; the unofficial modified public-defender form is never generated. The strongest available relief in Missouri comes with the strongest handoff: an incarcerated or supervised participant gets the attorney referral before the packet, not after it.

tracks.legalName: Expungement of Records on Stolen or Mistaken Identity (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 610.145)
tracks.publicName: You were named for someone else's case

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 610.145 was read verbatim from the Revisor's current text, effective 28 August 2017, and it contains two mechanisms rather than one. Subsection 1(1) is the petition: where a person is named in a charge for an infraction or offense, whether a misdemeanor or a felony, as a result of another person using the identifying information of the named person or as a result of mistaken identity, and the charges were dismissed or the person was found not guilty, the named person may apply by petition or written motion to the court where the charge was last pending, on a form approved by the office of state courts administrator and supplied by the clerk of the court, for an order expunging from all official records any entries relating to the person's apprehension, charge or trial. The court, after providing notice to the prosecuting attorney, shall hold a hearing and, upon finding that the person's identity was used without permission and the charges were dismissed or the person was found not guilty, shall order the expungement. Subsection 1(2) is the second mechanism and it needs no petition at all: where a person is named in a charge as a result of another person using their identifying information or of mistaken identity and the charge against the named person is dismissed, the prosecutor or other judicial officer who ordered the dismissal shall provide notice to the court of the dismissal, and the court shall order the expungement. Subsection 3 confirms the character of that second route by calling the beneficiary the person eligible for automatic expungement under subdivision (2) of subsection 1. Subsection 3 also directs the court to expunge its own entries and to direct all law enforcement agencies, the department of corrections, the department of revenue or any other state or local government agency identified by the petitioner — or by the person eligible for automatic expungement — to expunge their records, with the clerk notifying state and local agencies, and provides that the costs of expunging the records shall not be taxed against the person eligible for expungement under the section. Subsections 4, 5 and 6 supply substantial ancillary relief that the review did not carry: the department of revenue must expunge its entries, reverse administrative actions including licence points, suspensions and revocations, supply a certified corrected driver history at no cost and reinstate any licence at no cost; the department of corrections and any other agency must do the same and any reinstatement fee is waived; and any insurance company that charged an additional premium on insurance points from the expunged matter must refund those premiums for the three years before the expungement. Subsection 7 defines mistaken identity as erroneous arrest resulting from misidentification by a witness or law enforcement, confusion as to the identity of the person who committed the offense, misinformation provided to law enforcement as to that identity, or some other mistake on the part of a witness or law enforcement. The section is materially different from the § 575.120.4 identity-theft correction route on the CR300 form, which runs on a different statute, in a different court and division, and produces correction of the record to identify the actual defendant rather than expungement of entries relating to the participant.

units.label: Automatic expungement on prosecutor or judicial-officer notice — no participant filing
units.description: The first branch, and the statute itself calls it automatic. Under § 610.145.1(2), where the participant was named in a charge because another person used their identifying information or because of mistaken identity and that charge is dismissed, the prosecutor or other judicial officer who ordered the dismissal shall notify the court and the court shall order the expungement. There is no petition, no motion, no application and no form: the duty is on the prosecutor or the judicial officer, and § 610.145.3 confirms it by describing the beneficiary as the person eligible for automatic expungement under subdivision (2) of subsection 1. That has a direct product consequence, which is why this is a unit rather than a footnote: generating CR301 for a participant whose charge was dismissed on exactly this ground asks a court for relief the law has already told it to enter, and may cost them a filing fee for nothing. The unit's output is verification and explanation — check Case.net and the Highway Patrol record, ask the clerk whether an expungement order was entered on the dismissal, and understand that the participant may still identify agencies for the order to reach, because § 610.145.3 extends that right to the automatic beneficiary as well as to a petitioner. Where the order was not entered, the participant moves to the second unit.

units.label: CR301 petition to the court where the charge was last pending
units.description: The second branch: the participant's own petition or written motion under § 610.145.1(1), on OSCA CR301, filed in the court where the charge was last pending. It is the route where the participant was found not guilty rather than having the charge dismissed, since the automatic route reaches dismissals only; and it is the fallback where the charge was dismissed but the § 610.145.1(2) order was never entered. The form choice is not a preference: § 610.145.1(1) requires the application to be made on a form approved by the office of state courts administrator and supplied by the clerk of the court, so a custom pleading is not available here and official_pdf_fill is the only lawful strategy. CR301 is a single page with a short, factual allegation structure — the review calls it the cleanest form fill in Missouri and that is right. What it does not make easy is the proof: whether the participant's identity was used without permission, or whether a witness or law-enforcement officer made one of the four mistakes § 610.145.7 defines, is the finding the court must make, and the packet recites the participant's own account rather than characterising it.

geography.venue: The court where the charge was last pending (§ 610.145.1(1)). Where a case moved — from a municipal division to an associate circuit division, or between counties on a change of venue — it is the last court, not the first, and the participant confirms it from the docket. The automatic route has no venue because there is no filing; the court that took the dismissal is the court that orders the expungement.

destination.detail: Unit 2 is filed with the clerk of the court where the charge was last pending, and the clerk gives notice of the hearing to the prosecuting attorney, which is the whole of CR301's printed instruction to the clerk. § 610.145.3 makes the clerk responsible for notifying state and local agencies of the court's order. Unit 1 has no filing destination: the prosecutor or judicial officer notifies the court and the court orders expungement of its own motion.

components.notes: Unit 2's petition: Petition for Expungement — Mistaken Identity, OSCA (07-17) CR301, one page and fifty AcroForm fields. Note the source position, which is not the same as CR145, CR360 or CR375: this copy is held in the repository source corpus but is not retained by Master Library Edition 1.1, so it is an unmanifested asset carried on the pending-edition amendment ledger, and the Missouri Courts forms index reports the CR301 in its expungement set as updated 1 January 2025, which the corpus copy at revision 07-17 predates. The packet identity is settled and the source currentness is not. LegalEase completes the caption, the respondent agency block, and the identity and case block — full name, sex, race, date of birth, Social Security number, driver's licence number, address at the time of arrest, offense charged, date of arrest, and the case number and division of the court of the offense. The allegation that the participant's identity was used without permission, or that a witness or officer made one of the four § 610.145.7 mistakes, is recited from the participant's own words. The sworn statement and signature are left blank.

Unit 1 in full, plus the filing and follow-up instructions for unit 2, and the ancillary relief that most participants do not know exists. The verification sequence comes first: identify the case and the court where the charge was last pending; establish whether the charge was dismissed or you were found not guilty, because the automatic route reaches dismissals only; if it was dismissed on identity grounds, ask the clerk of that court whether an expungement order was already entered on the prosecutor's or judicial officer's notice; and check Case.net and the fingerprint-based Highway Patrol record. If the order was entered, no petition is needed and the participant's remaining task is to make sure the order reached the right agencies, which § 610.145.3 lets them identify. If it was not, unit 2's petition follows: file CR301 in the court where the charge was last pending, ask the clerk which case type code that court uses, and attend the hearing the court must hold after notice to the prosecuting attorney. The instructions then set out what the order does beyond the criminal record, because it is unusually broad and unusually easy to miss: the Department of Revenue must expunge its entries, reverse administrative actions including licence points and any suspension or revocation, supply a certified corrected driver history at no cost and reinstate any licence at no cost; the Department of Corrections and any other agency must expunge and reverse; any reinstatement fee is waived; and an insurer that charged extra premium on insurance points from the matter must refund three years of it on notification and verification. Finally, the costs of expunging the records are not taxed against the participant.

tracks._participantInputsNote: What LegalEase asks. Whether the charge was dismissed or ended in a not-guilty finding is asked first, because it decides which of the two units the participant is on.

participantInputs.question: How did the charge against you end — was it dismissed, or were you found not guilty at trial? If it was dismissed because of the identity problem, Missouri law says the prosecutor or judge should have told the court and the court should have expunged it without you filing anything.

Which happened? Did somebody else use your name, date of birth, Social Security number or other identifying information? Or was it a mistake — a witness or an officer misidentified you, was confused about who committed the offense, or was given wrong information about who it was?
In your own words, what happened? How did your name come to be on this case, and how did you find out?
What is your full legal name?
What is your date of birth?
CR301 asks for your sex and race. How would you like those answered?
What is your full Social Security number? CR301 asks for it on the face of the petition.
What is your driver licence number?
What was your address at the time of the arrest or apprehension?
What offense were you named in?
What was the date of the arrest or apprehension?
Which court was the charge last pending in, and in which county? If the case moved courts, it is the last one that matters.
What was the case number, and was it in the circuit, associate or municipal division?
Have you asked the clerk of that court whether an expungement order was already entered when the charge was dismissed?
participantInputs.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant reports the charge was dismissed rather than tried.

participantInputs.question: Which agencies do you believe hold records naming you on this case? § 610.145 lets you identify them and the order reaches every one you name — law enforcement agencies, the Department of Corrections, the Department of Revenue and any other state or local government agency.

Did this matter affect your driving licence — points, a suspension or a revocation? If so the order requires the Department of Revenue to reverse it and to give you a corrected driving history and a reinstatement at no cost.

Did your insurance premium go up because of insurance points from this matter? If so, the insurer has to refund the extra premium for the three years before the expungement once you notify and verify it.

What proof do you have that this was not you — a police report naming someone else, an identity-theft report, a letter from the prosecutor, a court entry, an alibi record? You do not need it to prepare the petition, but the court will want to see it.

rules.filing: Unit 2 is a petition or written motion filed in the court where the charge was last pending, on a form approved by the office of state courts administrator and supplied by the clerk (§ 610.145.1(1)). That statutory requirement is why the strategy is official_pdf_fill and not a custom pleading: the form is prescribed, not merely available. Unit 1 involves no filing at all. Whether the petition opens a new case or proceeds under the original number is local practice confirmed with the clerk.
rules.fees: The costs of expunging the records, as provided in chapter 610, shall not be taxed against the person eligible for expungement under this section (§ 610.145.3). Any reinstatement fee for a licence or privilege is waived (§ 610.145.5). Whether a court nonetheless collects an opening filing fee where the petition commences a new case is not addressed by the section and is confirmed with the clerk. No fee figure is published on this track.
rules.feeWaiver: Ordinarily unnecessary, because § 610.145.3 provides that costs are not taxed against the eligible person. GN10 under Rule 77.03 and § 514.040 is available where a court nevertheless requires an opening fee the participant cannot pay.
rules.notice: The court provides notice to the prosecuting attorney and shall hold a hearing on the motion or petition (§ 610.145.1(1)). rules.participantSignature: The petitioner swears or affirms under penalty of perjury that the facts are true according to their best knowledge and belief, and signs. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.

tracks._limitationsNote: Counsel approved this track with limitations. The composition is statutory: § 610.145 contains a petition and an automatic route, and only one of them produces a document.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The review identified two procedural paths and asked whether they are one track or two. Read against the verbatim text they are two legally distinct mechanisms inside one section, which makes this a composed route on the alternative mode rather than a split into two nodes or a single petition track with a footnote. § 610.145.1(1) is a participant petition on a form the statute requires the Office of the State Courts Administrator to approve and the clerk to supply. § 610.145.1(2) is automatic: the prosecutor or judicial officer who ordered the dismissal shall notify the court and the court shall order the expungement, with no petition, and § 610.145.3 confirms the character of it by naming the beneficiary the person eligible for automatic expungement under subdivision (2) of subsection 1. That is precisely the participant-filing-versus-automatic-relief pair composition exists for, and it has a real product consequence: generating CR301 for a participant whose charge was dismissed on identity grounds asks a court for relief the law already directed it to enter. The two are alternatives rather than stages because the automatic route reaches dismissals only, so a participant found not guilty is on the petition branch from the start. The petition unit is official_pdf_fill and could not lawfully be anything else, because § 610.145.1(1) prescribes the OSCA-approved form; a custom pleading is not available on this section. The track stays separate from the CR300 identity-theft correction route, which the adopted memorandum requires and which the forms themselves confirm: CR300 cites §§ 575.120.4 and 610.123, is filed in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of arrest, requires a fingerprint card, and corrects the record to identify the actual defendant. Different statute, different court, different division, different proof, different remedy.

controllingAuthority.summary: The review recorded the statutory basis and scope of CR300 as not established and made it the track's build blocker. It is now established, from the official form's own face and from the statute it cites. CR300 states: Pursuant to sections 575.120.4 and 610.123, RSMo, I hereby request that the court issue an order to expunge the following arrest and court records that falsely identify me and to correct the arrest and court records to accurately reflect the identity of the defendant. Its footer carries the same two citations. § 575.120 is the false impersonation offense, and subsection 4 supplies the victim's civil remedy: any person who is the victim of a false impersonation and whose identity has been falsely reported in arrest or conviction records may move for expungement and correction of those records under the procedures set forth in § 610.123, and upon a showing that a substantial number of identifying factors of the victim was falsely ascribed to the person actually arrested or convicted, the court shall order the false identifying factors contained in the arrest and court records amended to correctly and accurately identify the defendant and shall expunge the incorrect and inaccurate factors from the arrest and court records. That single provision answers every question the review left open. The relief is correction plus targeted expungement of the false identifying factors, not expungement of the case. The proof is a substantial number of identifying factors falsely ascribed, which is a different and in some ways lower showing than § 610.145's identity-used-without-permission finding. Relief is mandatory on that showing: the court shall order. The procedure is § 610.123's, which means a verified petition in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest, the eleven mandatory contents whose absence requires dismissal, the standard fingerprint card filed with the petition and forwarded to the central repository, defendants named with the order reaching only those named, and a hearing set no sooner than thirty days from filing with reasonable notice to each named entity. And critically the section reaches arrest or conviction records: unlike § 610.145 it does not require that the charge against the participant was dismissed or that they were acquitted, because the point is that somebody else was arrested or convicted under the participant's identity. The adopted Batch 2 memorandum's direction to keep this route separate from CR301 is therefore not merely preserved but strengthened: they are different statutes, different courts, different divisions, different proof and different remedies. The memorandum's primary-authority line cites § 610.145 for both forms; the form's own citation controls and is recorded as a correction.

provenance.sourceHeading: 10. Missouri — Track 8 — participant-facing output for identity-theft record correction
provenance.sourceStatement: OFFICIAL_PDF_FILL. CR300 is the statewide participant petition for correction of arrest/court records created through identity theft. It is distinct from CR301, which addresses mistaken identity. Keep the two routes separate, use the form matching the factual mechanism, and do not substitute a general § 610.140 expungement petition.

exclusions: A person who was not the victim of a false impersonation. § 575.120.4 opens the remedy to the victim of a false impersonation whose identity has been falsely reported in arrest or conviction records, so the predicate is that someone else used the participant's identity.
A record in which the participant's own identifying factors were correctly ascribed to the participant. The remedy corrects false identifying factors, so there must be something false to correct.
A showing that does not reach a substantial number of identifying factors falsely ascribed to the person actually arrested or convicted. A single coincident name is unlikely to meet it.

A case where the participant was themselves named in a charge because of misidentification by a witness or officer and the charge was dismissed or they were acquitted. That is § 610.145 relief on CR301, in the court where the charge was last pending, and it expunges entries relating to the participant rather than correcting the record to name someone else.

Federal records, which no Missouri court order reaches directly, although § 610.124 requires the central repository to ask the Federal Bureau of Investigation to expunge records expunged under § 610.123.

waitingPeriods.duration: none. Neither section states a waiting period. The remedy arises when the participant learns their identity has been falsely reported in arrest or conviction records.

geography.venue: The civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest (§ 610.123.1, incorporated by § 575.120.4), which CR300 states on its face: I am filing this petition in the county where the arrest occurred. This is the same court and division as the § 610.122 arrest route and is deliberately different from the § 610.145 mistaken-identity route, which goes to the court where the charge was last pending.

destination.name: Civil division of the Missouri circuit court in the county where the arrest occurred
destination.detail: Filed with the clerk of the circuit court, civil division, for the county of arrest, with the standard fingerprint card. CR300's printed instructions to the clerk direct that a copy of the petition be issued to each official, agency or other entity named in the petition; that a copy of the petition and the fingerprint card be sent to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository; and that notice of the hearing be given to the prosecuting attorney and to each official, agency or other entity named. The court sets the hearing no sooner than thirty days from filing under § 610.123.3.

components.notes: Petition for Correction of Arrest/Court Records — Identity Theft, OSCA (04-10) CR300, one page and fifty-four AcroForm fields, retained by Master Library Edition 1.1 as a source-gated asset rather than a packet-form candidate because its 2010 revision is currentness-gated. LegalEase completes the caption's judicial circuit and county with the case number, Court ORI number and Offense Cycle Number left for the clerk; the respondent block, which mirrors CR145's — circuit, associate and municipal court divisions, the criminal records repository, the county sheriff's department, the municipal police department, the Highway Patrol troop, the county or municipal prosecutor's office and free-text Other lines; the petitioner's identity block of full name, sex, race, date of birth, Social Security number, driver's licence number and address at the time of arrest; the arrest block of offense charged, date of arrest, citation number, any date of conviction, the county and municipality of arrest, the arresting agency, and the case number and division; and, where the participant knows them, the defendant's block of the impersonator's name, sex, race, date of birth, Social Security number and driver's licence number. The four printed recitals — that the participant is the victim of false impersonation and their identity has been falsely reported, that they have reason to believe the named respondents hold records, that the petition is filed in the county of arrest, and that they are providing fingerprints on a standard fingerprint card — are the participant's own sworn statements and the first of them is never asserted by LegalEase. The sworn-or-affirmed block and signature are left blank. Because CR300 is source-gated the packet identity is settled while the source is not, and the track cannot reach packet_ready until the current revision is confirmed.

components.conditionDescription: Generated where filing the petition opens a new civil case, which it ordinarily does since the participant was never a party to the underlying criminal matter.
components.notes: Confidential Case Filing Information Sheet. The Case Types List publishes no code naming § 575.120 or a record-correction petition, and its XG code is captioned Expungement of Crim/Arrest Record, which is the § 610.122 description. A June 2024 Missouri pro se guide reports practitioners filing identity-theft matters under X1, Other Miscellaneous Action, in the circuit column. The code is left as a manual completion item confirmed with the clerk, with X1 offered as observed practice. Note the privacy asymmetry on this route: the participant's own full Social Security number is on the face of CR300 because § 610.123.1(1)(f) makes it a mandatory content, and the impersonator's Social Security number may also be on the form where the participant knows it, so the confidentiality of the filing matters more here than anywhere else in the Missouri set.

The standard fingerprint card. § 610.123.1(7) makes the petitioner's fingerprints on a standard fingerprint card a mandatory content of the petition and directs dismissal where the information is not given, and CR300 recites it: I am providing my fingerprints on a standard fingerprint card for verification of my identity. On this route the card is doing more work than on any other, because the whole case is that the criminal record belongs to someone else and a fingerprint is the one identifier an impersonator cannot borrow. Obtained from a local law enforcement agency; three cards are wanted, one for the court, one for the clerk to send to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository and one for the participant. It is a required-before-filing item and never delays generation.

components.conditionDescription: Generated only where the participant answers that they cannot pay the filing fee and court costs.
components.notes: GN10 under Rule 77.03 and § 514.040. Worth generating by default as an option on this route: unlike § 610.145, neither § 575.120.4 nor § 610.123 exempts the petitioner from costs, so a victim of identity theft pays an ordinary civil filing fee to correct a record that was never theirs.

Sequenced participant instructions. Front-loaded: obtain three standard fingerprint cards from a local law enforcement agency, ringing ahead to confirm they will take three, the cost and the identification required; obtain a fingerprint-based Highway Patrol criminal record, which on this route is the central piece of evidence because a fingerprint-based search is the one search an impersonator's conduct cannot follow the participant into; and gather whatever identifies the person actually arrested or convicted. Then file in the civil division of the circuit court for the county of arrest with the fingerprint card and, where a new case is opened, FI-05 with the code the clerk confirms. The instructions reproduce CR300's printed instructions to the clerk so the participant can check the steps happened — the petition to each named entity, the petition and fingerprint card to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository, and hearing notice to the prosecuting attorney and each named entity — and explain the hearing is set no sooner than thirty days from filing. On the relief they are careful: what the court orders under § 575.120.4 is that the false identifying factors be amended to correctly and accurately identify the defendant, and that the incorrect and inaccurate factors be expunged from the arrest and court records. The case itself does not disappear; it stops being the participant's. The instructions also route the participant to the ordinary consumer identity-theft steps — a police report, a Federal Trade Commission identity-theft report, credit-bureau disputes — because a court order correcting a Missouri criminal record does not reach a private background-check database, and say plainly that the criminal correction and the consumer remedies are different problems.

tracks._participantInputsNote: What LegalEase asks. What distinguishes this from the mistaken-identity route is that somebody else was arrested or convicted using the participant's identity, so the questions reach the impersonator as well as the participant.

participantInputs.question: In your own words, what happened? Somebody else appears to have been arrested or convicted using your name or your identifying information. How did you find out, and what do you know about who it was?

Which of your identifying details appear on the record that is not yours — your name, date of birth, Social Security number, driver's licence number, address, or others? List every one, because the court has to find that a substantial number of your identifying factors were falsely ascribed to the person actually arrested or convicted.
What is your full legal name?
What is your date of birth?
CR300 asks for your sex and race. How would you like those answered?
What is your full Social Security number? On this route the law requires it on the face of the petition — § 610.123 says the petition shall be dismissed if it is not given.
What is your driver licence number?
What was your address at the time of the arrest recorded against your name? If you do not know, give the address you were living at then.
What offense is recorded against your name?
What is the date of the arrest recorded against your name?
In which Missouri county did that arrest occur, and if it was in a municipality, which one? This petition is filed in the circuit court for that county.
Which agency made the arrest?
What is the arrest citation number, if you know it?
participantInputs.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant has obtained the arrest record.

participantInputs.question: Was there a conviction on that record, and if so on what date? Unlike the mistaken-identity route, this one is available even where a conviction was entered — because it was entered against someone else.
What was the case number, which court and which division — circuit, associate or municipal?

If you know who used your identity, what are their full name, sex, race, date of birth, Social Security number and driver's licence number? Give only what you actually know. CR300 has a block for this and the court's order is meant to correct the record to name them.
participantInputs.conditionDescription: Asked where the participant reports knowing or believing they know who used their identity.

participantInputs.question: Do you know the person who used your identity — is it a family member, a former partner, or someone else you know? This changes both what evidence exists and what you should do next.

Which agencies hold the record that falsely identifies you? Include the court division, the arresting agency, the county sheriff's department, any municipal police department, the Highway Patrol troop, the Missouri Criminal Records Repository and the prosecutor's office.
The court's order will not reach any agency you do not name. Have you checked your Highway Patrol record and confirmed this list is complete?
Have you arranged to get three standard fingerprint cards from a local law enforcement agency? You need them before you file, and on this route they are the strongest evidence you have.
Have you reported the identity theft to the police, or filed a Federal Trade Commission identity-theft report?
Do you need to ask the court to let you file without paying the filing fee and court costs?

supportingDocuments.name: Three standard fingerprint cards
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: A local law enforcement agency — a municipal police department or county sheriff's department that takes applicant prints
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court filing, whether they can do three in one visit, the cost, the payment method and what identification to bring. § 610.123.1(7) makes the card a content of the petition, and CR300 recites that you are providing them for verification of your identity. One card goes to the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository, one is yours.

supportingDocuments.name: Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: Missouri State Highway Patrol, Criminal Justice Information Services Division, through the Missouri Automated Criminal History Site
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. This is the single most important document on this route: a name-based search will return the impersonator's conduct under your name, and a fingerprint-based search will not, so the difference between the two is itself evidence of what happened. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.

supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: The arresting agency, or the clerk of the court where the case was filed

You need to see exactly which of your identifying details were recorded, because the court's finding is about how many of your identifying factors were falsely ascribed to the person actually arrested or convicted.

supportingDocuments.name: Police report or Federal Trade Commission identity-theft report
supportingDocuments.obtainedFrom: Local law enforcement, or identitytheft.gov
supportingDocuments.conditionDescription: Where the participant has reported the identity theft, or is advised to.
supportingDocuments.howToObtain: File a report with local police and, separately, an identity-theft report with the Federal Trade Commission at identitytheft.gov. Neither is required by § 575.120.4, but both are ordinary corroboration and the Federal Trade Commission report is what you will need for the credit bureaus, which a Missouri court order does not reach.

rules.filing: A verified petition filed in the civil division of the circuit court in the county of the arrest, under the procedures set forth in § 610.123 as § 575.120.4 directs, on OSCA CR300, with the standard fingerprint card. § 610.123.1 makes eleven items mandatory contents whose absence requires dismissal, and the packet completes all of them from the participant's answers. § 610.123.5 directs the Supreme Court to promulgate procedures for cases filed under §§ 610.122 and 610.123 similar to the chapter 482 small-claims procedures.
rules.fees: Ordinary circuit court civil filing fees and costs, county-variable, confirmed with the clerk. Neither § 575.120.4 nor § 610.123 exempts the petitioner from costs, which is a real difference from the § 610.145 route where § 610.145.3 provides that costs are not taxed against the eligible person. The participant additionally pays for the fingerprint cards and for the Highway Patrol search. No fee figure is published on this track.
rules.feeWaiver: GN10 under Rule 77.03 and § 514.040, offered as an option rather than only on request, because no statutory fee exemption applies to this route.
rules.notice: The court sets a hearing no sooner than thirty days from filing and gives reasonable notice of the hearing to each official, agency or other entity named in the petition (§ 610.123.3). CR300's printed instructions to the clerk add that a copy of the petition is issued to each named entity, that a copy of the petition and the fingerprint card is sent to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository, and that hearing notice goes to the prosecuting attorney as well as to each named entity.
rules.service: None performed by the participant. The clerk issues the petition copies, sends the repository copy with the fingerprint card, and notices the hearing. CR300 carries no certificate of service.
rules.participantSignature: The petitioner swears or affirms under penalty of perjury that the facts are true according to their best knowledge and belief, and signs with their address. LegalEase leaves the signature and address line blank.
rules.notarization: none prescribed on CR300, which uses a sworn-or-affirmed statement rather than a notarial acknowledgment. This differs from CR145 on the § 610.122 route, which shares the same § 610.123 procedure but is subscribed and sworn before a notary, judge or clerk, and the difference is on the forms themselves rather than in the statute.

selfHelpStopConditions: The impersonator is a family member, a former partner or someone else known to the participant, which changes both the available evidence and what the participant should do next.
A conviction was entered under the participant's identity, particularly where a sentence was served or supervision imposed.
The participant has been arrested, detained or denied employment, housing or a licence because of the false record.
The prosecuting attorney or a named agency disputes the account, or the court sets a contested hearing.
The participant is unsure whether their situation is false impersonation under § 575.120 or mistaken identity under § 610.145, because the two run in different courts on different forms.
The record appears on a private background check after the court order, which a Missouri court order does not reach.
The participant is contemplating a civil claim against the impersonator or against an agency.
There are false records in more than one Missouri county, or in another state.
The participant is not a United States citizen or there is any immigration consequence.
The participant cannot obtain fingerprint cards from any local agency.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The adopted memorandum controls and directs official_pdf_fill on CR300, kept separate from CR301, using the form that matches the factual mechanism. That resolution is followed, and the review's build blocker — the statutory basis and scope of CR300, not established — is now closed from primary authority. CR300 says on its face and in its footer that it is brought pursuant to §§ 575.120.4 and 610.123. § 575.120.4 gives the victim of a false impersonation whose identity has been falsely reported in arrest or conviction records the right to move for expungement and correction under the § 610.123 procedures, and directs that on a showing that a substantial number of the victim's identifying factors was falsely ascribed to the person actually arrested or convicted the court shall order the false factors amended to correctly identify the defendant and shall expunge the incorrect and inaccurate factors. Everything the review could not answer follows from that: the scope is a record falsely identifying the participant, the remedy is correction plus targeted expungement rather than expungement of the case, relief is mandatory on the showing, the destination is the civil division of the circuit court in the county of arrest, the fingerprint card and the eleven mandatory contents come in through § 610.123, notice and the thirty-day hearing come in the same way, and the companion order is CR310. It also settles the separation the memorandum required more firmly than the memorandum itself did: this is a different statute from § 610.145, in a different court and division, on a different proof, producing a different remedy, and available even where a conviction was entered — because the conviction was somebody else's. The memorandum's primary-authority citation to § 610.145 for this form is recorded as a correction. CR300 remains source-gated: the retained revision is OSCA (04-10), the forms index reports the set as updated 1 January 2025, and the currentness could not be confirmed because the publisher blocks automated retrieval. Packet identity is settled; the source is not cleared.

limitations.statement: This route corrects a record so that it identifies the person actually arrested or convicted, and expunges the incorrect and inaccurate identifying factors. It does not make the case disappear. The packet says so plainly, because a participant told their record will be expunged and then shown the case still existing under someone else's name will reasonably feel misled.

tracks.legalName: Application for Expungement of a First Minor-in-Possession Violation (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 311.326)

controllingAuthority.summary: Section 311.326 was read in full from the Revisor's current text, effective 28 August 2009, and it is a single unnumbered paragraph that does a great deal of work. After a period of not less than one year after reaching the age of twenty-one, a person who has pleaded guilty to or been found guilty of violating § 311.325 for the first time, and who since that conviction has not been convicted of any other alcohol-related offense, may apply to the court in which he or she was sentenced for an order expunging all official records of the arrest, plea, trial and conviction. No records shall be expunged if the person is licensed as a commercial motor vehicle driver or was operating a commercial motor vehicle as defined in § 302.700 at the time of the violation. If the court determines, upon review, that the person has not been convicted of any other alcohol-related offense at the time of the application and has had no other alcohol-related enforcement contacts as defined in § 302.525, the court shall enter an order of expungement. The effect is to restore the person to the status occupied before the arrest, plea or conviction as if the event had never happened, with a perjury shield. A person is entitled to only one expungement under the section, and courts and other state officials may keep records necessary to enforce that limit. Three points are worth drawing out because the review left them open or unstated. Relief is mandatory: the court shall enter the order. The section says upon review rather than after hearing, which distinguishes it from § 610.130 and suggests no hearing is required, although it does not forbid one. And the alcohol-related enforcement contact condition borrows the same § 302.525.3 definition as § 610.130 — any suspension or revocation under §§ 302.500 to 302.540, any suspension or revocation in any state for refusing chemical testing under an implied consent law, and any conviction in any state involving driving while intoxicated, driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol, or driving with an unlawful alcohol concentration — so a participant with an administrative licence suspension that never became a conviction is ineligible even though nothing in the phrase alcohol-related offense would tell them so.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Both of the review's open questions are closed. No Office of the State Courts Administrator form exists for § 311.326 — a June 2024 Missouri pro se guide lists it, alongside § 610.130 and § 568.040, among the statutes for which no Missouri court forms are prepared and tells the reader to draft their own petition — so the output strategy is custom_pleading with localFormOverride, and the strategy is not left unresolved merely because the Office of the State Courts Administrator publishes nothing. And relief is mandatory: the section says the court shall enter an order of expungement where the conditions are found upon review. The statute supplies everything a pleading needs — who may apply, the age trigger, the conditions, the venue, the relief and its effect — and the pleading follows the OSCA pattern the review describes. And the waiting period runs from the participant's twenty-first birthday rather than from the offense or the conviction, so the earliest possible application is at twenty-two however old the case is. controllingAuthority.summary: The review's headline finding was that Missouri had passed Clean Slate provisions ten weeks earlier and that it could not confirm whether the Governor had signed the bill. That is now resolved from the enrolled text and the Governor's own record. Conference Committee Substitute for Senate Substitute for Senate Bill No. 1421, 103rd General Assembly, Second Regular Session, truly agreed to and finally passed as file 5940S.07T, was approved by Governor Mike Kehoe on 9 July 2026. It repeals fifty-four sections and enacts sixty-eight in lieu thereof, three of which are new chapter 610 sections: 610.141, 610.143 and 610.144. § 610.140 is not among the repealed sections and was not amended. § 610.141 is the mechanism. It defines an eligible offense as one that is a qualifying offense, is a final conviction, is the only charge of conviction in a case or part of a case containing only qualifying convictions, is one year past final disposition for a misdemeanor or three years for a felony, belongs to an offender with no misdemeanor or felony conviction within that same period excluding traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307, belongs to an offender with no outstanding arrest or pending charges at the time of analysis, and is not a class A felony. A qualifying offense is a conviction for possession of a controlled substance under § 195.202 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, unlawful use of drug paraphernalia under § 195.233 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, possession or control of a controlled substance under § 579.015, or unlawful possession of drug paraphernalia under § 579.074 — four offenses, nothing wider. Expungement is defined as closure of the record pursuant to § 610.120, so the legal effect is closure and not destruction. Final disposition means completion of all court-imposed terms and conditions and unconditional release from custody. Subsection 2 provides that all eligible offenses shall automatically be expunged as a matter of law upon eligibility and applies the section retroactively to any arrest, charge, trial or conviction for which there is an electronic record regardless of date. Subsection 3 puts the work on the central repository — the Missouri State Highway Patrol — which must screen the statewide criminal history database on a rolling basis not less than once per week, expunge eligible offenses, reflect the expungement through the Missouri uniform law enforcement system, rerun the analysis if further information is learned, and send the Supreme Court of Missouri a weekly list of changes. Subsection 4 requires the repository to notify the Office of the State Courts Administrator of its designations, makes the corresponding case records in the statewide court automation system confidential, and directs the Office of the State Courts Administrator to expunge those case records based only on the information in that system and the repository's designations. No participant submits anything at any point. Subsection 6 is the coordination answer the review flagged as a build blocker: an offender is limited to three misdemeanor and two felony expungements under this section and § 610.140 combined, and where a case contains more than one expungable offense only the highest-level offense counts. Subsection 7 preserves the right to file an expungement petition under any other law, and subsection 8 provides that notwithstanding any other provision of law the sole remedy for failure to expunge under the section is the filing of a § 610.140 petition. Subsection 10 is the timing provision: the provisions of the section shall be effective when technically feasible for both the Office of the State Courts Administrator and the central repository, but no later than 1 January 2027. Subsection 11 requires the Patrol to give consumer reporting agencies information sufficient to identify and delete records of expunged offenses, under an agreement restricting use and requiring destruction. Subsection 12 directs the Office of the State Courts Administrator, the Department of Corrections and the Patrol jointly to develop an explanatory document to be given at sentencing and on release from supervision. Subsection 9 requires annual statistical reporting to legislative committees beginning 1 January 2028. § 610.143 bars continued reporting of arrests, indictments and convictions once a pardon or expungement is known, gives the Attorney General enforcement powers and consumers injunctive relief, immunises employers, volunteer organisations and landlords who engage a person whose record was expunged absent a failure of reasonable care, and preserves mandatory disclosure for banking, insurance and § 610.120 contexts. § 610.144 creates the Missouri Expungement Fund to pay for the technology.

It states the law accurately and without promising anything: Missouri enacted state-initiated automatic expungement in 2026; the Governor approved the bill on 9 July 2026; the section operates when technically feasible for the Office of the State Courts Administrator and the central repository and no later than 1 January 2027; and as of the date the packet is generated neither body has published an implementation notice, eligibility instructions, a form, a portal or a schedule. It then explains what the section covers, which is far narrower than the headlines: four possession and paraphernalia offenses, one year after final disposition for a misdemeanor and three for a felony, only where the case contains no other kind of conviction, only where there has been no intervening conviction and no pending charge, and never for a class A felony. It explains what expungement means here — closure of the record under § 610.120, the same effect as a § 610.140 order rather than destruction. It explains that nothing is submitted and there is no way to apply, opt out or accelerate. And it puts the timing trade-off squarely, because that is the only decision the participant actually has: automatic relief costs nothing but is not yet demonstrably running and may not reach a given record, while a § 610.140 petition is available now, costs a filing fee and consumes a lifetime slot — and § 610.141.6 makes those slots shared, so a record cleared automatically uses one just as a petition does. The instruction is to check the Highway Patrol record after the section becomes operative rather than to wait passively, and it names the § 610.140 petition as the sole remedy for a failure to expunge, which is what § 610.141.8 provides.

participantInputs.question: Is the conviction for possessing a controlled substance, or for drug paraphernalia? Missouri's automatic expungement law reaches only those four offenses — it does not reach trafficking, distribution, delivery or manufacture.
Was it a misdemeanor or a felony? And if a felony, was it a class A felony? A class A felony is excluded.
On what date did you finish everything the court ordered and were released from any custody or supervision? The law calls that final disposition, and the one-year or three-year clock runs from it.
Was this the only conviction in that case? If the same case included a conviction for something that is not one of the four covered offenses, the automatic law does not reach any of it.
Since that date, have you been convicted of any misdemeanor or felony? Traffic regulation violations under chapters 301, 302, 303, 304 and 307 do not count.
Do you have any outstanding arrest, warrant or pending criminal charge right now?

Have you had any Missouri expungement before, under any law? From the date the automatic law starts operating, automatic expungements and petition expungements share the same lifetime limits — three misdemeanors and two felonies between them.

Do you need this record cleared by a particular date — for a job, a licence, housing or an immigration matter? The automatic mechanism has no published start date beyond a 1 January 2027 outer limit and cannot be relied on for a deadline.

Knowing that a petition under § 610.140 is available now but costs a filing fee and uses one of your lifetime slots, and that automatic relief is free but not yet shown to be running and uses the same slot, would you like to talk through which makes sense for you?

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The most time-sensitive Missouri question is resolved from primary authority and the answer is that the law exists. CCS SS SB 1421 was truly agreed to and finally passed in the 2026 Second Regular Session and approved by Governor Kehoe on 9 July 2026, enacting §§ 610.141, 610.143 and 610.144. § 610.140 was not amended. So this is not failed legislation and the source slot is not a rejected or monitoring-only node: there is a real, enacted record-clearing mechanism and it is represented as a relief track. The output strategy is process_guidance, and the ground is the narrowest and strongest one available: § 610.141 creates no petition, application, request, opt-out or acceleration, and puts the entire mechanism on the central repository and the Office of the State Courts Administrator. There is genuinely nothing for a participant to file, which is what keeps the track off the guidance re-review queue — not agency control, not discretion, not a future implementation date. The build blocker the review flagged on cap coordination is closed by § 610.141.6, which limits an offender to three misdemeanor and two felony expungements under §§ 610.140 and 610.141 combined, so an automatic expungement does consume the same lifetime slot a petition would; the § 610.140 packet now carries that as an instruction. The legal effect is closure under § 610.120, not destruction, because the section defines expungement that way. What remains open is operation. Subsection 10 makes the provisions effective when technically feasible for both bodies and no later than 1 January 2027, and neither the Highway Patrol nor the Office of the State Courts Administrator has published an implementation notice, eligibility instructions, a form, a portal or a schedule. The adopted memorandum requires an administering-agency implementation notice before this route is released, and that condition is not met, so the track stays disabled on a precisely stated operational gate rather than on an unanswered question about whether the law exists. The review's instruction is honoured in both directions: the packet does not tell a participant their drug offense will clear itself, and does not tell them it will not. And because a § 610.140 petition remains available and § 610.141.8 makes it the sole remedy for a failure to expunge, the participant is never told to wait without being told what waiting costs and what the alternative is.

limitations.statement: The scope is four offenses, not a category. § 610.141 reaches possession of a controlled substance under § 195.202 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, unlawful use of drug paraphernalia under § 195.233 as it existed prior to 1 January 2017, possession or control of a controlled substance under § 579.015, and unlawful possession of drug paraphernalia under § 579.074. Trafficking, distribution, delivery and manufacture are outside it, and Missouri must never be described as a general clean-slate state.
